title: Define the loop and stop condition for a refund agent
persona: Meera, PM on a refunds desk at a quick-commerce app
scenario: You're specifying an agent that processes refund requests end to end: read the ticket, pull the order, check the policy, decide, and either issue the refund or explain the decline. In testing it loops — re-reading the same order, re-checking the same policy, occasionally issuing two refunds for one order. It has tools for order lookup, policy lookup, refund issuance and ticket reply. Issuing a refund moves real money and cannot be undone from inside the agent.
badPrompt: write a prompt for a refund agent that handles refund requests
badOutput: You are a helpful refund assistant. Read the customer's request, look up their order, check our refund policy, and decide whether to issue a refund. Be polite and empathetic. If a refund is warranted, issue it. Otherwise explain why not.

hints.title: Name the terminal states
hints.body: A loop ends when it reaches a state you listed. Refund issued, refund declined with reason, escalated to a human — and nothing else counts as done.

hints.title: Double refunds are an idempotency bug
hints.body: Say that issuance must be checked against what has already been issued for this order, and that a second issuance needs a human.

checks.tip: Describe it as a loop with defined steps, not a vibe.
Inventory the tools the agent actually has.
Describe the observed failure: looping and double issuance.
State that issuance is irreversible and must not repeat.
Ask for an idempotency guard before issuance.
Require an escalation path when the policy is ambiguous.
Specify a structured spec: states and transitions.
Bound the loop: a maximum number of steps before forced escalation.

tipIfLow: A loop without terminal states is just a while(true). Strong version: 'Specify the control loop for a refund agent with four tools: order lookup, policy lookup, refund issuance, ticket reply. It currently re-reads the same order, re-checks the same policy, and has issued two refunds for one order. Define: the ordered steps, the exact terminal states (issued / declined with reason / escalated), an idempotency check that must pass before issuance, a maximum step count after which it escalates rather than continuing, and the rule that issuance is irreversible so any second attempt on an order goes to a human. Output as states and transitions, not prose.'
goldPrompt:
You are helping me specify an agent's control loop. I'm Meera, PM on a quick-commerce refunds desk.

The agent has exactly four tools: order_lookup, policy_lookup, issue_refund, reply_to_ticket. Issuing a refund moves real money and CANNOT be undone from inside the agent.

Observed failures in testing: it re-reads the same order, re-checks the same policy, and has issued two refunds against a single order.

Specify the loop:
1. The ordered steps, and the precondition for each.
2. The exact terminal states. I believe they are: refund issued, refund declined with a reason given to the customer, escalated to a human. Tell me if a fourth is genuinely needed; do not invent one otherwise.
3. An idempotency guard that must pass before issue_refund is called, given that a second issuance on the same order is always a bug.
4. A step budget, after which it escalates rather than continuing.
5. The ambiguity rule: when policy does not clearly cover the case, escalate rather than deciding.

Output as a state-and-transition table, not prose. For each transition, name the tool call that triggers it. Flag any step where you are assuming behaviour I have not described.
